channel.title: Audi recalls — Car Recall Tracker
channel.description: NHTSA vehicle safety recalls explained in plain English.

item.title: Audi Q5, SQ5 Seat Belts May Not Restrain
item.description: Some Audi Q5, Q5 Sportback, SQ5, and SQ5 Sportback vehicles may have driver and front passenger seat belts that were manufactured incorrectly. Because of this manufacturing problem, the affected seat belts may not properly hold the driver or front passenger in place during a crash. This means the seat belts may not restrain these occupants as they are designed to.

item.title: E-Tron Sportback brake pedal may detach
item.description: On some E-Tron Sportback vehicles, the fastener connecting the brake pedal to the brake booster may not have been properly assembled. This can cause the brake pedal to detach from the booster, which can cause a loss of braking and increase the risk of a crash.

item.title: Audi A6, A7, Q8 Lane Departure Warning May Deactivate
item.description: These Audi vehicles were already repaired earlier under a different recall. Because of a software error, the lane departure warning system, the feature that alerts the driver if the car drifts out of its lane, may be switched off. The driver may not realize the system is off and may count on warnings that will not come. A dealer will update the software to correct it.

item.title: Audi rearview camera may fail to show image
item.description: Audi is recalling certain 2019 through 2026 vehicles, including A6, A7, Q7, Q8 and e-tron models. A software error can keep the backup camera picture from showing on the screen the way it is supposed to. Because the rear camera view may not appear, these vehicles do not meet the federal safety rule covering what a driver must be able to see behind the vehicle.

item.title: Audi E-Tron Models: Rear Seat Belt May Not Lock
item.description: Audi is recalling certain 2025 SQ6 E-Tron, SQ6 Sportback E-Tron, Q6 Sportback E-Tron, A6, A5, A6 Sportback E-Tron, Q6 E-Tron, S5, and S6 Sportback E-Tron vehicles. The automatic locking retractor on the rear seat belts may fail to engage when a child seat is installed using the seat belt. Because of this, the vehicles do not meet federal occupant protection and seat belt standards.

item.title: Audi Q7 and Q8 Seat Belt Buckle Missing Rivet
item.description: On certain 2025 Audi Q7, Q8, RS Q8, and SQ8 vehicles, the seat belt buckle for the driver or front passenger may be missing a rivet. This rivet is what attaches the buckle to the seat belt stalk. Without it, the buckle may not properly secure the seat belt in place.

item.title: Audi S6 Sportback Seat Belts May Fail
item.description: Some Audi and Volkswagen vehicles, including the Audi S6 Sportback e-tron, have a seat belt problem. A metal bar inside one or both front seat belt retractors may have been damaged during manufacturing.

item.title: Audi SQ7 Fuel Pump May Cause Leak
item.description: An Audi SQ7 vehicle has a fuel system problem. The bolts holding the high-pressure fuel pump in place may not be tightened correctly, which can cause a fuel leak.

item.title: Audi Q5 Cylinder Head Cover Screws Can Loosen
item.description: The screws that hold the cylinder head cover in place on these SUVs may not have been tightened correctly at the factory. Over time, those screws can work themselves loose. Once they loosen, engine oil can start to leak out from under the cover. An oil leak like this raises the chance that a fire could start.

item.title: Audi Q6 e-tron rearview camera image may be delayed
item.description: Audi is recalling certain 2025 Q6 and SQ6 vehicles. After the driver shifts into reverse, the picture from the rearview camera may be delayed or may switch off. That means the screen may not show what is behind the vehicle when it is needed. Because of this, these vehicles do not meet the federal rear visibility standard. Dealers will update the software in the rearview camera control unit free of charge, and owner letters were mailed May 20, 2025.

item.title: Audi Q6 e-tron and SQ6 e-tron blurry rearview camera
item.description: The rearview camera may show a blurry image, giving the driver a less clear view of what is behind the vehicle.

item.title: Audi Models: Instrument Panel Display May Fail
item.description: Due to a software error, the instrument panel display on affected vehicles may fail, meaning it can stop showing information to the driver.

item.title: Audi Q4 E-Tron, VW ID.4 Can Lose Drive Power
item.description: In certain Audi Q4 e-tron, Q4 e-tron Sportback, and Volkswagen ID.4 vehicles, the onboard charger that keeps the 12-volt battery charged can fail and stop charging that battery. When the 12-volt battery isn't being charged, the vehicle can lose the power that drives it, meaning the car could suddenly stop moving forward while you are out on the road.

item.title: Audi Q5 High-Voltage Battery May Overheat
item.description: In these Audi Q5 and A7 E Hybrid vehicles, the high-voltage battery that powers the car can overheat. An overheating high-voltage battery like this creates a risk of fire, according to the notice.

item.title: Volkswagen Tiguan and Audi Q3 rearview camera may not display
item.description: Volkswagen is recalling certain Tiguan and Arteon vehicles and certain Audi Q3 vehicles. The control unit that runs the backup camera can hit an error when the vehicle is started, and when that happens the rearview camera image does not show up the way it should. Because of this, these vehicles do not meet the federal government's rear visibility safety standard. Dealers will install updated software for the camera control unit free of charge.

item.title: Audi Q5 Hybrid Battery May Overheat And Catch Fire
item.description: Certain Audi Q5 and A7 plug-in hybrid vehicles have a high-voltage battery that may overheat. An overheating high-voltage battery increases the risk of a fire starting in the vehicle. This affects the battery that powers the vehicle's electric drive system.

item.title: Audi E-Tron GT Battery Short Circuit Fire Risk
item.description: Audi says the high-voltage battery in some E-Tron GT and RS E-Tron GT vehicles may develop a short circuit inside a battery module. Dealers will install new diagnostic software as the fix. Until then, some vehicles will have their battery data monitored online at no cost; if a problem is found, the owner will be told to charge only to 80% capacity until the module is replaced. Vehicles without online monitoring will get a dealer inspection instead.

item.title: Audi E-Tron Brake Pedal May Detach
item.description: A bolt that connects the brake pedal to the brake booster may not have been properly installed during manufacturing. If this fastener fails, the brake pedal can come apart from the brake booster. When that happens, the vehicle can lose its ability to brake normally, which increases the risk of a crash. Dealers will inspect the brake booster and repair it as needed, free of charge.

item.title: Audi E-Tron GT Front Brake Hose Can Leak
item.description: On these cars, the brake hoses that run to the front wheels can develop tears. A tear can let brake fluid leak out, which can cause that brake circuit to stop working properly. When this happens, the brake pedal may need to be pushed down farther than normal, and the brakes may not slow the car as well as they should, making it take longer to come to a stop.

item.title: Audi Q4 E-Tron Headlight Software Issue
item.description: Some Q4 E-TRON and Q4 E-TRON Sportback vehicles may have had the wrong headlight control module software installed. Because of this, the parking lights may not work as intended when the headlights are on and the turn signals are activated.

item.title: Audi SUVs and A4 Allroad Risk Passenger Airbag Shutoff
item.description: An electrical connection in the front passenger seat for the occupant detection system may loosen. If it loosens, the system can deactivate the front passenger air bag, meaning the air bag would not be active for that seat.

item.title: Audi E-Tron GT High-Voltage Battery Fire Risk
item.description: In these electric Audis, the high-voltage battery pack may develop a short circuit inside its battery modules.

item.title: Audi, VW Fuel Tank Seal May Cause Leaks
item.description: Volkswagen is recalling certain front-wheel-drive Audi A3, Volkswagen Golf, Golf Sportwagen, GTI, and Jetta vehicles. A seal on a suction jet pump inside the fuel tank may fail, allowing fuel to flow into the evaporative emissions system and possibly leak out of the charcoal canister. A fuel leak near a source of ignition can increase the risk of a fire. Dealers will replace the suction pump. This recall replaces an earlier recall, so vehicles already repaired under it will need the new repair.

item.title: Audi Q7 and Q8 Side Airbag Mounting
item.description: The side air bag built into the driver's seat may not have been properly mounted to the seat's frame during assembly. Because it isn't attached the way it should be, the air bag may not work as intended if it needs to deploy.

item.title: Audi E-Tron High-Voltage Battery May Overheat
item.description: Some Audi E-Tron vehicles have a high-voltage battery that may overheat. Dealers will install onboard software that keeps an eye on how well the battery modules are performing. If a module is found to have a problem, dealers will replace it. This applies to the E-Tron Sportback Quattro and E-Tron Quattro models covered by this recall, and the work will not cost owners anything. Audi has already begun mailing notification letters to owners about this issue.

item.title: Audi portable charging cables can overheat and cause fire
item.description: Audi is recalling certain electric and other models over the portable charging system supplied with the vehicle. When the industrial 220-volt/240-volt plug is used at the 100% charge setting, some home outlets cannot handle the electrical current the charging system needs. The outlet or the charging cable can then overheat. Dealers will supply a new 220-volt/240-volt portable charging cable with a temperature sensor built in, free of charge.

item.title: Audi A6, A7, S7 Wrong Brake Fluid Cap Risk
item.description: Some of these Audi vehicles may have a brake fluid reservoir cap that was installed with the wrong label. Because the cap's label does not match what should be used, it is possible for the wrong type of brake fluid to end up in the vehicle. Using the incorrect brake fluid can reduce how well the brakes work, making the vehicle less able to slow down or come to a stop when needed.

item.title: Audi Q7 Windshield Camera Heater May Overheat
item.description: In certain 2020 Audi Q7 vehicles, the software that controls the front camera isn't compatible with the heating element built into the windshield for that camera. This mismatch can cause the heating element to overheat. An overheated heating element raises the chance that a fire could start.

item.title: Audi Liquid Spill Can Cut Engine Power
item.description: If liquid is spilled in the back seat, it can leak into a part called the gateway control module and cause it to shut down. When this control module shuts down, it can suddenly reduce how much power the engine is producing while the vehicle is being driven.

item.title: Volkswagen and Audi Tire Pressure Monitor Software Issue
item.description: Your vehicle's tire pressure monitoring system is supposed to warn you when tire pressure gets too low. In these vehicles, if all four tires lose air pressure at the same time, the system may not detect this quickly enough to warn you. This means you might not get a timely alert if every tire loses pressure at once. Dealers will fix the problem by updating the tire pressure monitoring software at no cost.

item.title: Audi Rearview Camera Display May Stop Working
item.description: On a range of Audi models, the infotainment system's main unit can become damaged internally when the vehicle is shut off. When this happens, the rearview camera image will not display the next time the vehicle is started, and the vehicle no longer meets the federal rule requiring a working rear visibility display.

item.title: Audi Q5, VW Atlas Engine Bearings May Fail
item.description: Some Audi Q5 and Volkswagen Atlas and Atlas Cross Sport vehicles may have damaged connecting rod bearings inside the engine. Damaged bearings can cause the engine to fail while driving. If the engine failure also causes an oil leak, that leak can raise the chance of a fire.

item.title: Audi backup camera screen may go blank in reverse
item.description: Volkswagen is recalling certain 2021 and 2022 Audi cars and SUVs because of a software problem with the backup camera display. When the vehicle is put into reverse, the screen may go blank or black instead of showing the view behind the vehicle. Because of this, the vehicles do not meet the federal safety rule for rear visibility. Dealers will update the software in the infotainment unit, the system that runs the center screen.

item.title: Audi Q3 fuel may spill from filler neck
item.description: Volkswagen is recalling certain 2021 and 2022 Audi Q3 vehicles. A vent pipe inside the fuel tank may have been damaged while the tank was being assembled. If that pipe is damaged, gasoline can spill out of the filler neck when someone opens the fuel cap. Dealers will inspect the vent pipe inside the tank and, if it is damaged, replace the charcoal canister and the fuel tank, all free of charge. Notification letters were mailed November 1, 2022.

item.title: Audi Q7 and Q8 fuel pump may fail
item.description: Volkswagen is recalling certain Audi Q7 and Q8 SUVs because a component inside the fuel pump can break. When that happens, the fuel pump can fail.

item.title: Audi A6, A7, S6, S7 Fuel Level Sensor Problem
item.description: In some Audi A6, A7, S6, and S7 vehicles, the fuel level sensor in the tank may stick. This can cause the fuel gauge on the instrument cluster to show an inaccurate reading, so it may not reflect how much fuel is actually in the tank. Because the gauge can be wrong, a driver may run out of fuel without realizing it, which can cause the engine to stall while driving.

item.title: Audi rear axle alignment may not have been checked
item.description: Volkswagen is recalling certain 2019 through 2021 Audi cars and SUVs, including A4, A5, A6, A7, A8, Q5, Q7, Q8 and S and RS versions. These vehicles had repairs done under an earlier recall, and the rear axle alignment may not have been checked afterward as it should have been. Rear axle alignment that is off can wear the tires out early or wear them unevenly.

item.title: Audi Q5 and SQ5 water damage may cut power
item.description: This recall covers certain Audi Q5 Sportback, SQ5 Sportback, Q5, and SQ5 vehicles. A liquid spill in the rear seat, or water getting in through a gap in the underbody seam, may reach the gateway control module and cause it to shut down.

item.title: Audi passenger airbag may be switched off by faulty cable
item.description: Audi is recalling certain 2017-2020 cars because of a fault in the cable that connects the passenger seat heater to the system that detects whether someone is sitting in the front passenger seat. A poor connection can make the software read a fault that is not there and switch off the passenger airbag. Dealers will replace the cable and either the seat heating mat or the whole seat cover. This recall expands an earlier recall, and vehicles already repaired under that one need to return for the new repair.

item.title: Audi Rearview Camera May Not Display When Reversing
item.description: On some Audi vehicles, a software error may prevent the rearview camera image from displaying when the vehicle first starts to reverse. The video feed meant to show what's behind the vehicle while backing up may not appear right away.
